subject: research/simdesign-edgescan
professional: a senior finite-element / stress analyst doing a mesh-convergence (solution verification) study of a stress concentration; first checks: where the peak sits and how it is sampled (centroid vs surface), whether the quantity converges under refinement (Richardson / GCI, ASME V&V 20), and whether the conclusion about 'noise' versus systematic discretisation error is supported by the meshes run

evidence.correctness: Reproduced the headline experiment: copied the subject to scratchpad, `python experiments/edgescan.py` (scikit-fem 12.0.2, scipy 1.18.1, 4 cores, 50 s) wrote an edgescan.txt that `diff`s IDENTICAL to the committed one, and edgescan.json max |diff| 0.0 MPa with every feasibility flag equal. Recomputed the README's derived statistics with my own script from the JSON (scratchpad/simdesign-edgescan/stats.py; numpy.polyfit deg 2): residual SD 2.38/1.63/1.79, 1.70/1.56/1.50, 1.39/1.09/0.92 MPa match the README's 2.4/1.6/1.8, 1.7/1.6/1.5, 1.4/1.1/0.9; upward-step counts 2..6; largest up-step 6.38 MPa (h=1.5, r=8) and 0.64 at h=0.75 r=14; five feasibility flips at h=1.5 r=8. Independent hand checks: profile mass by area formula L*w + (H-w)*w + r^2(1-pi/4) at w=16.5, r=8, b=2, rho=7.85e-3 -> 37.39 g (README 37.39); plane-stress lambda* = 2*lam*mu/(lam+2mu) and the plane-stress von Mises sqrt(sxx^2 - sxx*syy + syy^2 + 3 sxy^2) match the textbook forms (Timoshenko & Goodier); nominal beam bending 6F(L-w/2)/(b w^2) = 79.06 MPa at w=16.5, so the FE peak 98.75 implies Kt 1.25 at r/w ~ 0.5, a plausible fillet factor; tip deflection 0.292 mm vs 0.329 mm from centreline Euler-Bernoulli (two arms, F(L-w/2)^3/3EI + F(L-w/2)^2(H-w/2)/EI), FE 11% stiffer as a rigid corner predicts. The numbers the scan reports are what the model produces and the model is right as a P2 plane-stress solve; the defect is in what the peak measure means (domain), not in the arithmetic.
evidence.completeness: README Method and Reproduce checked: 189 solves, 21 widths, three h, three r all present in the JSON; `pytest -q tests` -> 7 passed in 11.7 s (README says 7 tests, a few seconds); experiment 50 s (README about 45 s). The quadratic-detrend residual SDs and the 6.4/0.6 MPa largest-step figures in the README are not produced by any committed code (`grep -rn 'polyfit\|residual\|std' experiments src` empty); they recompute correctly but a reader cannot regenerate them from the repo. Next steps (patch measure, topology test, mesh offsets) are honestly listed as not done.
evidence.verification: `pytest -q tests` 7 passed. Four seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: shear stress factor (model.py:128) caught; edge() break->continue (edgescan.py:32) caught; deleting the plane-stress lambda conversion (model.py:102, i.e. silently solving plane strain) SURVIVED; removing the clamp-zone exclusion from the peak mask (model.py:131) SURVIVED. Tests check only orderings (wider -> lower stress, finer -> higher) and one feasibility flag; no test pins a stress, deflection or mass against an analytic value, and nothing tests the README's statistics.
evidence.craft: Read model.py, dfm.py, measures.py, edgescan.py, test_edgescan.py. model.py:105 `fb = ... if False else None` and :107 an unused `fb` are dead code; Material defaults and docstring (model.py:18) still describe an FDM thermoplastic in a steel-sheet project; make_mesh sets d=None when grid*boundary >= 4e7 points and then evaluates `d > 0.6*h` (model.py:71-73), so any h <= ~0.35 mm crashes: ran solve(h=0.3) -> TypeError "'>' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'float'". The experiment mutates the module global dfm.MAX_SLENDER inside each worker (edgescan.py:297) instead of passing a parameter. The whole model is a copied engine (one of ~55 simdesign-* copies), by design per the README.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'Peak stress is not monotone in w' backed by edgescan.txt (pass). Residual SDs backed by recomputation, not by a file (partial). 'The largest single upward step is ... 0.6 MPa at the finest case (h=0.75, r=14)' is true but selective: at the same finest mesh r=8 the largest step is 2.10 MPa (partial). 'Peak von Mises at a re-entrant corner is a singular-ish quantity' is wrong for this geometry: the corner carries an 8-14 mm fillet and the peak sits on the fillet arc (w=16.5 r=8: peak at (16.39, 22.37), on the arc ending at (16.5, 24.5)), a smooth stress concentration that should converge (fail). The headline 'the refinement effect reported in simdesign-widerweb ... is not separated from mesh noise' fails when the mesh is refined further (domain). Disclaimer and 'stylised, preliminary' labelling present. Live page not loaded (proxy 403 on marisstella.app).
evidence.fitness: A researcher building on this would take away that the feasible edge is a ~0.5 mm band set by jitter and that refinement beyond h=1.0 no longer moves it. Both are undermined by two more meshes: at r=8 the edge is 17.0 at h=0.75 but peak at w=17.0 is 102.04 MPa at h=0.5 and 103.65 at h=0.4 (infeasible), and at h=0.4 the edge is between 17.3 (100.33) and 17.5 (98.01) mm. The systematic drift (+5 MPa from h=0.75 to 0.4 at fixed w) is several times the 0.9-1.4 MPa jitter. Nearest prior work: in-repo simdesign-meshconverge already reported the peak measure not converging to h=0.5 (not engaged here beyond 'through it'); outside, solution-verification practice (Roache's grid convergence index, 1994; ASME V&V 20) and superconvergent patch recovery (Zienkiewicz & Zhu 1992) are the standard tools for exactly this question and none is cited. Not new and the main conclusion is not sound.
evidence.domain: A stress analyst would first ask where the peak is sampled: here at P2 element centroids, i.e. ~h/3 inside the free surface at a fillet where the true maximum is on the surface. Under-reading shrinks as h shrinks, so the peak rises monotonically with refinement (w=16.5 r=8: 98.75, 104.65, 105.57, 107.73, 109.07 MPa at h=1.5, 1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.4; ran scratchpad/simdesign-edgescan/conv.py) and has not converged at 0.4 mm. The project attributes the shift to noise and calls the corner singular-ish; the method departs from standard practice (surface/nodal stress recovery or extrapolation, a refinement sequence with GCI) and its conclusion reverses on the next two meshes. The jitter observation itself (centroid position moving relative to the arc as w changes) is real but its cause was not tested.

Peak is sampled at P2 element centroids, ~h/3 inside the fillet surface, so it under-reads the surface maximum by a mesh-dependent amount; no surface/nodal recovery or extrapolation, no GCI
README calls the corner re-entrant and its peak 'singular-ish'; the corner has an 8-14 mm fillet and the peak lies on the arc, a smooth concentration that should converge

No prior work on solution verification cited (Roache GCI, ASME V&V 20, Zienkiewicz-Zhu recovery), and the in-repo simdesign-meshconverge finding that peak stress does not converge to h=0.5 is not engaged
Residual-SD and largest-step statistics in the README are computed by no committed code
'0.6 MPa at the finest case (h=0.75, r=14)' picks the smallest of the three finest-mesh series; r=8 at h=0.75 has a 2.10 MPa step
make_mesh sets d=None for large grids and then compares it, so solve() crashes with TypeError for h below ~0.35 mm, blocking the very refinement this study needs
Tests pin no numeric value: silently solving plane strain or dropping the clamp-zone exclusion leaves all 7 green
Dead code (`if False else None`, unused fb) and FDM-plastic Material defaults in a steel-sheet model

verdict: simdesign-edgescan scans the feasible web width of a stylised 2 mm laser-cut steel L-bracket at 0.1 mm steps on three meshes. Its numbers reproduce exactly (re-run diffed identical; residual SDs, step counts and the mass recompute independently; the FE solve agrees with beam theory and gives a plausible fillet Kt of 1.25). It does not meet the bar because its conclusion does not survive the obvious next check a stress analyst would make: the peak is read at element centroids inside the fillet surface, so it rises steadily with refinement (98.4 -> 103.7 MPa at fixed w from h=0.75 to 0.4) and the 'edge' moves another ~0.4 mm, a systematic drift several times the jitter the README says swamps it. The corner is mislabelled singular, standard solution-verification practice is not cited, two of four seeded mutants survive, the mesher crashes below h~0.35 mm, and the README's statistics come from no committed code. A faithful observation of centroid jitter, not yet a sound result to build on.
